editorial:
Ever wondered what happens when a legendary filmmaker gets obsessed with a master painter? You get a fascinating look at Orson Welles and his deep love for Francisco Goya. This documentary feels less like a boring history lesson and more like a conversation between two geniuses from different centuries. It shows how Welles saw Goya not just as an artist, but as a rebel who wasn't afraid to show the dark side of human nature. The vibe is curious and respectful, making you feel like you are uncovering a secret friendship through old clips and art pieces.

What really works here is how it connects the dots between cinema and painting without getting too stiff. The pacing is steady, and while it might feel a bit slow if you want a thrill ride, the visual reveals are great. If you enjoy art or old Hollywood, you will love this. It is best viewed in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to really see the details in Goya's paintings. If you prefer owning your movies, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your physical collection is a smart move for the high image quality.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up by showing how Goya's influence stayed with Orson Welles until the very end of his life. It explains that Welles viewed the painter as a kindred spirit who fought against the rules of his time. The final scenes connect the dots between Goya's dark sketches and Welles' own style of storytelling. It ends on a thoughtful note, leaving you to realize that true art never really dies.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves art history, classic movies, or the life of Orson Welles.
